prompt_title: Need a different way to take part? (optional)
prompt_a: During the claim sort, point, say, sign or show the adult an idea, question or change that would help. You may pass or speak privately. The adult listens, explains what can change and checks whether it helped.
prompt_b: While reviewing your evidence, point, say, sign or show the adult an idea, question or change that would help. You may pass or speak privately. The adult listens, explains what can change and checks whether it helped.
review_intro: Use your existing results or the clearly labelled model data. Point, speak, sign, draw or use your current work; no extra feedback form is needed.
review_steps: Choose one conclusion. Show the adult which results support it. Name the surfaces and whether the evidence is measured or model data.
Consider the feedback. Does the conclusion fit both trials? Check one control or uncertainty; a surprising result is not automatically wrong.
Keep or improve your explanation and show why. The adult responds to your idea or question. Keep the original results; label any later retry separately.
review_close: You may ask for more thinking time, use a trusted adult or pass. Finish with the existing exit question; this review stays within its four minutes.
staff_sections: Use regulation time, a trusted adult, accessible response routes and permission to refuse. The small help prompt is optional; useful feedback remains part of ordinary teaching. Refusal is information, not a reason to invent a response or punish passing.
Lesson A: a claim worth revisiting

During We Do 2, invite a pupil to identify one word or idea in a sorted claim that needs checking. Hear, read or watch the response. Use the actual surface-pair example to adapt the explanation, scaffold or next question. Keep this within the existing eight minutes of sorting and correction, then use two minutes for the exit.

After the 32-minute workshop, use four minutes to revisit one conclusion and its supporting results with the adult, then four minutes for the exit. Use the existing record or an equivalent response; do not require a separate loop sheet. Explain any limit on a requested change and check whether the response helped.

Space makes participation possible; Voice is the pupil's response in their own modality; Audience requires the adult to engage with it; Influence is the resulting adjustment to explanation, task, scaffold or subsequent teaching. One optional displayed prompt does not limit genuine feedback exchanges.

Use R only after a pupil response and genuine adult engagement. A click, download, opened explanation or completed exit does not automatically establish Audience, Influence, R or an assessment outcome. Record only the evidence and help actually provided; do not require a duplicate written record for every task. Use agreed policy codes appropriately. Extended writing or assessment may need one or two precise next steps and response time.

Feedback & Marking Policy 2025/2026 (Pilot), Issue 1, May 2026; master order §25.3. Lesson A remains 40 minutes. Lesson B remains 32 + 4 + 4 minutes. No extra pupil form, signature, standalone participation stage or progression gate is required.
